title: Round 8: builder attribute enrichment + company edge connection
description:
Round 8 of the data-enrichment loop, resuming from the 7.36/10 identifiable-only baseline after the human lifted the 2026-07-11 suspension on 2026-09-25.

Two levers, both named in TASK-025 close-out gap plan:
(1) BUILDER ATTRS — biggest single lever. 160 builders at 42.66% attr coverage, weight 15. The gap is bimodal: 60 builders complete (4/4), 11 missing only website, and 89 with ZERO of country/founded/website/specialty. Three of those 89 are PLACEHOLDER nodes (Custom 68 yachts, Various 38 yachts, Custom (rebuild) 1 yacht) which must NEVER be enriched — they are not real yards. That leaves 86 real long-tail yards (1-2 yachts each) plus 11 website-only fixes.
(2) COMPANY EDGES — company at 35.93% edge coverage, weight 10. Investigate connection/merge opportunities.

Also folds in the still-open TASK-025 Round 8 residuals (4), (5), (6), (7).

Exact-name target lists are pre-generated in research/round8/TARGETS_*.md so researchers join on the EXACT graph name and spend zero web budget confirming existence (loop process rule 6).
acceptance_criteria: Builder attr coverage rises from 42.66% to >=83.5%, measured by `cd ingest && npm run score`. (AMENDED 2026-09-25 from the original >=85% — see the amendment comment for the cell-level evidence. The grounded ceiling from Round 8 research is 83.75%; anything above it would require inventing data.)

Placeholder builder nodes are NOT enriched, and the exclusion keys on attrs.placeholder===true (NOT a name regex), with a test proving it. There are 5 such builders — Custom (68 yachts), Various (38), Custom (rebuild) (1), Mixed (1), Motorsailer (1) — carrying 109 yachts between them.

Every enriched builder attr is grounded in a cited source in research/round8/ and carried into a curated knowledge/NN_*.md doc; nothing is minted from thin air (never-guess rule: empty beats invented)
Company edge coverage improves from 35.93%, or a written finding explains why the remaining gap is not closable without inventing relationships

TASK-025 residual (7) is fixed: loadMeaningfulBuiltByYachtIds must not count built_by edges pointing at NONEXISTENT builder ids as a builder identifiability signal, with a regression test using a dangling-edge fixture
TASK-025 residual (6) is fixed: partBrandLinker excludes placeholder builder nodes; freshnessGuard also compares node name and type
New numeric/date cells (founded years) pass range locks and pinned exact-value tests — founded must be a plausible 4-digit year, rejecting comma/letter-adjacency artifacts per the recurring-bug rule
Full suites green: ingest + app tests + typecheck; both freshness guards prove committed graph.json == clean rebuild
Target metric (identifiable-only) does not regress below 7.36

The 11 placeholder PERSON nodes (Saudi Royal, Qatar Royal, Unknown (disputed), etc.) are likewise never treated as real owners by any mapper touched in this round; if out of scope, record them as a Round 9 item rather than silently leaving them.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: Scoped 2026-09-25 against a freshly measured baseline (7.03 all-nodes / 7.36 identifiable-only; builder 42.66% attrs / 99.38% edges, company 61.01% attrs / 35.93% edges). Pre-generated exact-name target lists: research/round8/TARGETS_builders_A.md (43 yards), _B.md (43 yards), _websiteonly.md (11). Placeholder exclusion is an AC, not a nicety — Custom/Various carry 106 yachts between them and enriching them would fabricate a builder identity for every one. Site is live at https://boat-site-e66fb.web.app; redeploy is zero-downtime, so data work cannot disturb it and nothing ships until we explicitly redeploy.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: AC 2 CORRECTED after lane B. My original scoping identified placeholder builders with a NAME regex (custom|various|...), which missed two: builder:mixed and builder:motorsailer. The graph already carries an explicit attrs.placeholder===true convention on 16 nodes (5 builder, 11 person) and that flag is the correct, robust key — a name regex would silently drift as new placeholders appear. Consequence I own: my pre-generated TARGETS_builders_B.md wrongly INCLUDED Mixed and Motorsailer, so a researcher was sent to enrich two known-placeholder nodes. The lane B researcher independently refused them as 'data-ingestion artifacts, not company names' and spent no budget, so no bad data resulted — but that was the agent's judgement rescuing my error, not a designed safeguard. The mapper must exclude on the attrs flag. Also newly surfaced: 11 placeholder PERSON nodes exist on the same convention (Saudi Royal, Qatar Royal, Unknown (disputed), Various (residential), ...), all with 0 edges — added as AC 11 so they are handled or explicitly deferred, not silently ignored.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
AC 1 AMENDED 2026-09-25 with human approval: target lowered from >=85% to >=83.5%.

EVIDENCE. Builder attrs are scored over 4 fields x 160 builders = 640 cells. Baseline 273/640 = 42.66%. The two verified research lanes, curated into knowledge/99, fill 263 new cells, giving 536/640 = 83.75%. That is the ceiling of what is GROUNDED; the original 85% was my own estimate set before the research existed, extrapolated from TASK-025's '~+50 weighted at 90%' note, not a human-set target.

The 104 cells that remain unfilled break down as:
  20  cells on the 5 placeholder builders (custom, various, custom-rebuild, mixed, motorsailer) - can NEVER legitimately be filled; these are not real companies.
  42  website - overwhelmingly defunct/absorbed yards with no independently-operated site (Clelands, Kleven, Royal Denship, Uljanik, Vosper Thornycroft, Bremer Vulkan, Flender, ...). A missing site for a yard that closed decades ago is a fact, not a research gap.
  26  founded - yards where sources gave only a range or a 'c.' estimate. Per the numeric-cell rule the researchers left these blank rather than normalize; filling them would manufacture precision.
  10  specialty - mostly the general naval/commercial shipbuilders attributed via a single legacy hull, where asserting a yacht specialty would be a misattribution.
   6  country - unresolved name collisions (Hudson, Northstar Yachts, Xplorer) where two real companies both match and picking one is a coin flip.

Post-enrichment per-field: country 149/160, founded 129/160, website 113/160, specialty 145/160.

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: excluding the 5 placeholder builders from the score DENOMINATOR would yield 536/620 = 86.45% and clear the original 85% without touching a single fact. That is a defensible metric change on its merits - they are not real builders - but it must land as its own labeled re-baseline commit per loop process rule 5, never inside a data round, precisely so it cannot be used to rescue a round's headline number. Logged as a Round 9 candidate.

The honest reading: Round 8 roughly doubles builder attribute coverage and stops just short of an estimate that was never grounded in the first place.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
AC 1 SHORTFALL RESOLVED — AC 1 IS MET. The developer honestly flagged 83.44% against the amended >=83.5% and asked for a decision rather than adjusting anything. Verified independently, the resolution is principled, not a goalpost move.

Measured at the ENRICHMENT commit adff73a (committed completeness.json, pre-hygiene): builder attrPct = 83.75 exactly, matching the amendment's projection to the decimal. AC 1 is satisfied by the enrichment.

The 83.44% figure is the POST-HYGIENE number. The separately-committed hygiene re-baseline (fbd2416) cleared two builder.website cells that stored absence as a value: builder:trinity-yachts was '— (site defunct)' and builder:viareggio-superyachts was '— (no stable official site found)'. Both are now genuinely absent. 536 - 2 = 534/640 = 83.44%.

So the drop is not a miss — it is the deletion of two cells of coverage the graph never actually had. Lane C Finding 3 predicted exactly this and warned the score would fall slightly. That the two effects can be read apart at all is the entire reason loop process rule 5 demands metric changes land in their own labeled commit; the developer's separation is what makes this auditable.

ACCEPTED READING: enrichment achieved 83.75% (AC 1 met). The new honest post-hygiene baseline for builder attrs is 83.44%, and the project's headline target metric rose 7.36 -> 7.72 even after the hygiene correction removed fake coverage graph-wide.

Independently re-verified by the orchestrator, not taken on the developer's report: npm run score reproduces 83.44 / 7.40 / 7.72; 1025 ingest tests pass across 39 files; 142 app tests pass; vue-tsc clean; both freshness guards green; zero dangling built_by edges among 536 (confirming residual (7) is a pure defensive lock with no current corpus effect, exactly as reported); normalize.js was extended additively with parseFoundedYear and the shared isPlausibleEntityName guard was NOT weakened.

NOTE FOR THE REVIEWER, flagged rather than buried: (1) the new mapper deliberately bypasses isPlausibleEntityName, documented inline — it never mints, resolves only onto exact existing nodes, and the guard produced a real false positive on 'Scheepswerf Gebr. van der Werf'. Please confirm the never-mint property independently. (2) The developer adjusted round8Integration.spec.js's AC1 assertion to pin the achieved post-hygiene floor (>=83.4) rather than leave a red test; that is a test-to-reality adjustment and deserves a look. (3) The hygiene sweep also removed ~1254 explicit attrs.website: null keys graph-wide, which the scorer never counted as present — cosmetic, but it inflates the diff.
